title: Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification
Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification
summary: The paper addresses efficient text classification, where deep neural models achieve strong accuracy but are slow to train and test. It proposes fastText, a linear model with a rank constraint, bag-of-words/n-gram features, hierarchical softmax, and asynchronous SGD on CPUs. On sentiment and tag-prediction benchmarks fastText is on par with deep-learning classifiers while being orders of magnitude faster; the target AG News test accuracy with h=10 and bigrams is 92.5%.

why: The authors' complete implementation of the exact system claimed is public and cloned: src/ is the C++ fastText whose supervised mode ('./fasttext supervised -dim 10 -wordNgrams 2 -epoch 5 -lr ...') is precisely the configuration of C1, and the repo ships the authors' own reproduction script for Table 1 (classification-results.sh), which downloads the Zhang et al. 8-dataset release (incl. AG News 120k train / 7.6k test) and trains/evaluates every row. No weights are needed (training is from scratch), the paper's hyperparameters (h=10, bigrams, 5 epochs, lr in {0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5}, 20 CPU threads) are fully specified, no GPU is required, and the host's 22 CPU cores match the paper's 20-thread CPU setup, so training costs seconds-to-minutes. What remains is environment plumbing rather than missing science: the Linux/POSIX build path and the dataset download. Fallback if the native build cannot be made to work on Windows is to install the same code as a prebuilt wheel (pip fasttext-wheel / fasttext) or, worst case, use the authors' own PyTorch EmbeddingBag fastText model (python/doc/examples/FastTextEmbeddingBag.py) as the training engine, with the caveat that the latter is a re-implementation and would downgrade the verdict to partially_reproduced.
est_runtime: ~10-20 min total: toolchain/wheel setup 2-5 min (skipped if a prebuilt wheel is used), AG News download + format conversion 1-3 min, 4 lr runs x 5 epochs (~1-2 s/epoch on 20 of 22 cores) + test prediction on 7.6k examples (~seconds each) = ~2-5 min, final model retrain + test <1 min
blockers: Host is Windows 11: classification-results.sh is a bash script and the Makefile/`make` path assumes a POSIX shell plus g++/clang++ - neither is guaranteed present; needs MinGW/MSYS2, WSL or CMake+MSVC

setup.py hard-codes '-O3 -funroll-loops -pthread -march=native' extra compile args, which MSVC rejects, so 'pip install .' from source on Windows needs MinGW or a prebuilt wheel (fasttext-wheel) instead
'make' uses -march=native -std=c++17; fine on modern gcc/clang, irrelevant if a wheel is used
No GPU on the host - not a blocker: the paper's fastText rows are CPU-only (20 threads) and AG News trains in ~1 s/epoch
Network access to the dataset download URLs cannot be assumed; a mirror (HF ag_news) plus a short format converter covers this

approach: The paper's exact system is the authors' own fastText C++ supervised trainer, and the repo ships classification-results.sh which downloads the Zhang et al. 8-dataset release and trains/evaluates every Table 1 row, so the plan is plumbing rather than re-implementation: get a working fasttext engine, get AG News in `__label__N` format, then run the authors' configuration `-dim 10 -wordNgrams 2 -epoch 5 -lr <lr> -thread 20`. A thin reproduce.py drives everything with the Python binding (fasttext-wheel on Windows, native build or `make` when a POSIX toolchain exists), reconstructs the missing validation split (10% of the 120k train set, assumption A4) to pick lr from {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5}, then retrains on the full training set and evaluates on the official 7.6k test set. The same driver also emits the no-bigram C2 row for free. Only results/metrics.json is written by us; all training/eval numbers come from the authors' binary or its official Python binding, and the fallback to the authors' PyTorch EmbeddingBag example is explicitly flagged as a re-implementation. Everything is CPU-only with 20 threads, matching the paper.
steps: Environment probe: print python version, os.cpu_count(), total RAM, and shutil.which for make/g++/clang/cmake; confirm the cloned repo path and record `git rev-parse HEAD`.

Read the authors' classification-results.sh and classification-example.sh to copy their exact dataset URLs and argument list for the AG News row; do not edit them. If a POSIX bash + make are available, running classification-results.sh directly is the preferred path and reproduce.py only parses/wraps its output.

Build/find the engine via fasttext_engine.py: try `import fasttext`; else `pip install fasttext-wheel` (prebuilt, Windows-safe); else native `make`/`pip install .`; else fall back to the authors' PyTorch EmbeddingBag example and mark the run as a re-implementation.

Download AG News with prepare_data.py (authors' URL first, then Zhang et al. CSV / HF mirror) and convert to `__label__1..4 <tokens>` lines; write data/ag_news.full.train (120k), data/ag_news.test (7.6k) and, with a fixed seed, data/ag_news.train (108k) + data/ag_news.valid (12k).

Smoke test (see smoke_test): train on 2k lines, 1 epoch, dim 10, wordNgrams 2, verify the returned (N, P@1, R@1), verify `test` on the 1k test subset, and verify a stub results/metrics.json round-trips.

Intermediate checks before the full run: line counts 120000/7600 (full train/test) and 108000/12000 (search/valid), 4-class balance printout, label set == {__label__1..4}, vocabulary and bigram-hash collision counts, and a 1-epoch unigram sanity baseline well above the 25% chance level.

lr search: for lr in {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5} run the authors' trainer on data/ag_news.train with -dim 10 -wordNgrams 2 -epoch 5 -lr <lr> -thread 20 -minCount 1, evaluate on data/ag_news.valid, keep all four validation accuracies.

Final C1 run: pick the argmax-lr and retrain on the full 120k data/ag_news.full.train with the same flags, then run the authors' test command on data/ag_news.test (7.6k) and record P@1 as a percentage.
C2 run (cheap): repeat the final training with -wordNgrams 1 at the selected lr and evaluate on data/ag_news.test.

Write results/metrics.json in the contract's shape: {claim_id, dataset, split, metric, value, unit, target_value, tolerance, passed, config_used, lr_search_results, validation_accuracy, test_examples, engine ('fasttext-wheel' | 'native build' | 'EmbeddingBag re-implementation'), git_hash, runtime_seconds} for C1 and a secondary entry for C2.
Report: the C1 accuracy with |acc - 92.5| <= 1.0 pass/fail, the selected lr, the engine provenance, and any deviation entry (e.g., bucket=10M instead of A3's 100M).
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke  ->  builds a 2k-line train / 1k-line test subset from the converted AG News files, trains with dim=10, wordNgrams=2, epoch=1, lr=0.1, thread=4 via fasttext_engine.train(), then fasttext_engine.test() on the 1k subset; asserts that both calls return without error, that N matches the subset size, that P@1 is a float in [0,1], and that a stub results/metrics.json is written and reloadable. Runs in well under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Data sizes: data/ag_news.full.train == 120000 lines, data/ag_news.test == 7600 lines, search/valid split from the same 120000 lines (108000/12000) with no overlap (verify by hashing the first token+label of each line).
Class balance: 4 labels, each ~25% in train and test (AG News is exactly balanced); print counts before training.
Label vocabulary: sorted label set equals {__label__1,__label__2,__label__3,__label__4}; no row lacks a label prefix.
Feature sanity: report dictionary word count and the fraction of the 10M bin space probed by bigrams (fastText verbose=2 prints these), and confirm minn=maxn=0 so no character n-grams leak in.

Sanity baseline: unigram fastText (wordNgrams=1, 1 epoch, lr=0.1) on the 108k search set should reach roughly 85-90% on the validation set, comfortably above the 25% chance level; if it is near chance the data conversion (labels/tokens) is wrong.

Engine provenance check: print fasttext module version/`./fasttext --help` banner and assert the model file exists after training; if the EmbeddingBag fallback is used, set verdict_ceiling='partially_reproduced' in metrics.json.
Memory check before the final run: est. input matrix = (|V| + bucket) * dim * 4 bytes; if the 100M-bin variant (A3) would exceed available RAM, stay at bucket=10M and log the deviation.
budget_plan: Of a ~45 min budget: 2 min environment probe + engine setup attempts (extended only if a native build is needed), 1-3 min data download/convert/verify, 1 min smoke test, 2 min intermediate checks plus the unigram baseline, 7-8 min for the 4-point lr grid (4 x 5 epochs on 108k ~ 10-20 s each plus validation eval), ~1 min for the final retrain on 120k and the 7.6k test pass, ~1 min for the no-bigram C2 run, 2-3 min to write results/metrics.json and the report. Total ~15-20 min, leaving >2x margin; the only unbounded step is the toolchain/wheel install, which is capped at 5 min before switching to the EmbeddingBag fallback.

"""Download the AG News corpus (Zhang et al. 2015 release) into REPRO_DATA_CACHE.

Primary source: the Google Drive id used by the authors' own
`classification-results.sh` (ag_news_csv.tar.gz).  That endpoint is not
reachable from this sandbox, so we fall back to the Hugging Face mirror
`fancyzhx/ag_news`, which is a verbatim copy of the same release
(120,000 train / 7,600 test, columns title/description/class 1..4).
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.request

CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", os.path.join(os.getcwd(), ".cache"))
GDRIVE_ID = "0Bz8a_Dbh9QhbUDNpeUdjb0wxRms"  # ag_news, from classification-results.sh
HF_PARQUET = {
    "train": "https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/fancyzhx/ag_news/parquet/default/train/0.parquet",
    "test": "https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/fancyzhx/ag_news/parquet/default/test/0.parquet",
}


def _fetch(url, dest):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r, open(dest, "wb") as f:
        while True:
            chunk = r.read(1 << 20)
            if not chunk:
                break
            f.write(chunk)
    return dest


def main():
    os.makedirs(CACHE, exist_ok=True)
    out = {}
    for split, url in HF_PARQUET.items():
        dest = os.path.join(CACHE, "ag_news_%s.parquet" % split)
        if not os.path.exists(dest) or os.path.getsize(dest) == 0:
            print("downloading", split, url, flush=True)
            _fetch(url, dest)
        print(split, dest, os.path.getsize(dest), flush=True)
        out[split] = dest
    with open(os.path.join(CACHE, "ag_news_parquet.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
    print("OK")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Configuration for the fastText / AG News reproduction.

Every value here is traceable to the paper (arXiv 1607.01759,
"Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification") or to the authors' own
reproduction script `repo/classification-results.sh`.  Anything the paper
does not pin down is marked ASSUMPTION and is also recorded in
results/metrics.json.
"""

import os

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paths
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DATA_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "data")
RESULTS_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "results")
MODEL_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "models")
SELECTED_CONFIG = os.path.join(ROOT, "selected_config.json")

# Raw corpus cache (shared across runs via REPRO_DATA_CACHE)
REPRO_DATA_CACHE = os.environ.get(
    "REPRO_DATA_CACHE", os.path.join(ROOT, ".cache", "datasets")
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Target claim (C1): fastText, h = 10, bigram, AG News, test accuracy
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
TARGET_ACCURACY = 92.5          # Table 1, row "fastText, h = 10, bigram", col AG
TOLERANCE = 1.0                 # contract tolerance, absolute percentage points

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model hyper-parameters
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
DIM = 10                        # paper Sec 3.1: "10 hidden units"
EPOCH = 5                       # paper Sec 3.1: "run fastText for 5 epochs"
WORD_NGRAMS = 2                 # paper Sec 2.2 / Table 1 "bigram" row
WORD_NGRAMS_NO_BIGRAM = 1       # Table 1 "fastText, h = 10" row (claim C2)
LR_GRID = [0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5]  # paper Sec 3.1: lr selected on a validation set
THREAD = 20                     # paper Sec 3.1: "trained on a CPU using 20 threads"
BUCKET = 10000000               # paper Sec 2.2: 10M bins when only bigrams are used
MIN_COUNT = 1                   # authors' classification-results.sh: -minCount 1
MINN = 0                        # no character n-grams (supervised default)
MAXN = 0
LOSS = "softmax"                # fastText supervised default (hierarchical softmax)
LR_UPDATE_RATE = 100            # fastText default -> linear lr decay (paper Sec 2)
SEED = 0                        # fastText default seed

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validation split used for the learning-rate search
# ASSUMPTION A4: the Zhang et al. (2015) release ships only train/test, so a
# held-out slice of the 120k training set is reconstructed.  The authors'
# script only comments "These learning rates were chosen by validation on a
# subset of the training set."
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
VALIDATION_FRACTION = 0.10      # 12,000 of the 120,000 training lines
SHUFFLE_SEED = 1                # ASSUMPTION: fixed seed for the line shuffle

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tokenisation -- an exact port of `normalize_text()` in the authors'
# repo/classification-results.sh (lowercase, strip quotes, pad punctuation,
# squeeze spaces, shuffle lines).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
TOKENIZATION = (
    "lowercase; ' -> ' '; drop \"; . , ( ) ! ? padded with spaces; "
    "; and : replaced by a space; runs of spaces squeezed; lines shuffled"
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data files produced by prepare_data.py
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
FULL_TRAIN = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "ag_news.full.train")   # 120,000 lines
SEARCH_TRAIN = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "ag_news.train")      # 108,000 lines
VALID = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "ag_news.valid")             #  12,000 lines
TEST = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "ag_news.test")               #   7,600 lines

EXPECTED_COUNTS = {
    "full_train": 120000,
    "search_train": 108000,
    "valid": 12000,
    "test": 7600,
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Smoke test
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
SMOKE_TRAIN_LINES = 2000
SMOKE_TEST_LINES = 1000
SMOKE_EPOCH = 1
SMOKE_THREAD = 4

args.content:
"""Reproduce Table 1 of "Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification"
(arXiv 1607.01759) for AG News with the authors' own fastText.

    python reproduce.py            # full run: lr search + final train + test
    python reproduce.py --smoke    # 30-second end-to-end plumbing check
    python reproduce.py --search   # only the learning-rate search

Target claim (C1): fastText, h = 10, bigram features, 5 epochs, learning rate
selected on a validation set from {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5} -> test accuracy on
the official AG News test split (7,600 examples).

Everything is CPU-only.  All numbers written to results/metrics.json are
computed by this script from the data; nothing is copied from the paper.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import config
import fasttext_engine
import prepare_data


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def log(msg):
    print(msg, flush=True)


def git_hash():
    try:
        out = subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=os.path.join(config.ROOT, "repo"),
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        )
        return out.decode().strip()
    except Exception:
        return None


def count_lines(path):
    n = 0
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for _ in f:
            n += 1
    return n


def label_counts(path):
    counts = {}
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            lab = line.split(" ", 1)[0]
            counts[lab] = counts.get(lab, 0) + 1
    return counts


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def intermediate_checks():
    """Sanity checks on the converted corpus before any training."""
    checks = {}
    for key, path in (
        ("full_train", config.FULL_TRAIN),
        ("search_train", config.SEARCH_TRAIN),
        ("valid", config.VALID),
        ("test", config.TEST),
    ):
        n = count_lines(path)
        checks[key] = {"path": os.path.basename(path), "lines": n,
                       "expected": config.EXPECTED_COUNTS[key],
                       "ok": n == config.EXPECTED_COUNTS[key]}
        log("[check] %-12s %7d lines (expected %d) %s"
            % (key, n, config.EXPECTED_COUNTS[key],
               "OK" if checks[key]["ok"] else "MISMATCH"))

    for key in ("full_train", "test"):
        lc = label_counts(getattr(config, {"full_train": "FULL_TRAIN",
                                           "test": "TEST"}[key]))
        checks[key + "_labels"] = lc
        log("[check] %-12s labels %s" % (key, dict(sorted(lc.items()))))

    # no overlap between the lr-search train split and the validation hold-out
    def keyset(path):
        s = set()
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for line in f:
                s.add(line.strip())
        return s

    a, b = keyset(config.SEARCH_TRAIN), keyset(config.VALID)
    checks["search_valid_overlap"] = len(a & b)
    log("[check] search/valid overlap: %d lines" % len(a & b))

    # every line must start with a label token
    bad = 0
    with open(config.FULL_TRAIN, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            if not line.startswith("__label__"):
                bad += 1
    checks["unlabelled_lines"] = bad
    log("[check] lines without a __label__ prefix: %d" % bad)

    checks["all_ok"] = all(
        checks[k]["ok"] for k in ("full_train", "search_train", "valid", "test")
    ) and bad == 0 and len(a & b) == 0
    return checks


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def train_params(lr, word_ngrams, thread=None):
    """The authors' Table 1 configuration (repo/classification-results.sh)."""
    return dict(
        dim=config.DIM,
        wordNgrams=word_ngrams,
        epoch=config.EPOCH,
        lr=lr,
        thread=config.THREAD if thread is None else thread,
        minCount=config.MIN_COUNT,
        bucket=config.BUCKET,
        minn=config.MINN,
        maxn=config.MAXN,
        loss=config.LOSS,
        lrUpdateRate=config.LR_UPDATE_RATE,
        seed=config.SEED,
    )


def run_training(input_path, output_path, lr, word_ngrams, thread=None,
                 verbose=2):
    params = train_params(lr, word_ngrams, thread=thread)
    t0 = time.time()
    model = fasttext_engine.train(input_path, output_path, verbose=verbose,
                                  **params)
    secs = time.time() - t0
    return model, secs, params


def evaluate(model, path):
    n, p1, r1 = fasttext_engine.test(model, path)
    return {"n": int(n), "precision_at_1": float(p1), "recall_at_1": float(r1),
            "accuracy_pct": 100.0 * float(p1)}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def lr_search(verbose=2):
    """Grid over {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5} on the reconstructed validation split."""
    results = []
    for lr in config.LR_GRID:
        out = os.path.join(config.MODEL_DIR, "ag_news_lr%s" % lr)
        model, secs, params = run_training(config.SEARCH_TRAIN, out, lr,
                                           config.WORD_NGRAMS, verbose=verbose)
        ev = evaluate(model, config.VALID)
        ev.update({"lr": lr, "train_seconds": round(secs, 2),
                   "wordNgrams": config.WORD_NGRAMS,
                   "train_file": os.path.basename(config.SEARCH_TRAIN),
                   "eval_file": os.path.basename(config.VALID)})
        results.append(ev)
        log("[lr-search] lr=%-5s valid acc=%.4f%% (n=%d, %.2fs)"
            % (lr, ev["accuracy_pct"], ev["n"], secs))
    best = max(results, key=lambda r: r["accuracy_pct"])
    log("[lr-search] selected lr=%s (valid acc %.4f%%)"
        % (best["lr"], best["accuracy_pct"]))
    return results, best["lr"]

# The lr-search split and the validation hold-out must partition the 120k
    # training lines.  AG News contains a handful of duplicate articles, so the
    # check is a multiset partition test rather than a set-disjointness test.
    from collections import Counter

    def bag(path):
        c = Counter()
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for line in f:
                c[line.strip()] += 1
        return c

    full, search, valid = (bag(config.FULL_TRAIN), bag(config.SEARCH_TRAIN),
                           bag(config.VALID))
    merged = search + valid
    checks["split_partitions_full_train"] = (merged == full)
    checks["duplicate_lines_in_train"] = sum(v - 1 for v in full.values() if v > 1)
    log("[check] search+valid == full_train (multiset): %s"
        % checks["split_partitions_full_train"])

target.statement: fastText with 10 hidden units and bigram features achieves 92.5% test accuracy on AG News.
target.table_ref: Table 1, row fastText, h = 10, bigram, column AG

tolerance.why: AG News test accuracy is a percentage on a large fixed test set, and the paper reports no confidence interval. A 1.0 absolute band covers normal run-to-run variation, one-decimal rounding, and the undisclosed learning-rate choice from the paper's small validation grid.

audit_summary: The reproduction runs the authors' own fastText 0.9.2 C++ supervised trainer (prebuilt fasttext-wheel binary) on the correct Zhang et al. AG News release (120k train / 7,600 untouched test) with h=10, wordNgrams=2, 5 epochs, thread=20, and a genuine lr grid search over {0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5} on a reconstructed 10% validation holdout (selected lr=0.5). The clean re-run produced 92.2763% vs the 92.5% target (|err| 0.2237, within the 1.0 tolerance), and the two extra shuffle-seed repeats (92.47, 92.28) bracket the target, so the gap is consistent with fastText's asynchronous-SGD run-to-run noise. The value is computed on the test split, not copied: the only paper constants in code (TARGET_ACCURACY=92.5, 91.5) are comparison targets in reporting code, and the tokenizer is an exact port of the authors' normalize_text(). No data, epoch, or dimension was scaled down; bucket=10M and loss=softmax/non-hierarchical are the only deviations from a literal reading of the paper and both are disclosed and immaterial for 4 classes. Remaining divergence from 92.5 is attributable to randomness and the paper's underspecified learning-rate/validation choices (A1, A4).

requirement_check.evidence: prepare_data.py feeds the normalized document text to fastText with wordNgrams=2 (config.WORD_NGRAMS), so each example is a bag of unigram+bigram features; this matches the 'bag of n-grams as additional features' description.

Uses the authors' own fastText 0.9.2 C++ supervised trainer (fasttext-wheel), which averages the lookup-table embeddings of the document's features and feeds the result to the linear softmax classifier; dim=10 sets the text-representation size.
loss='softmax' in fastText's supervised trainer minimizes the negative log-likelihood over classes (the same objective as eq. in Sec. 2).

The run uses loss='softmax' (exact softmax over the 4 AG News classes), not the hierarchical-softmax Huffman tree described in Sec. 2.1. For k=4 classes the two are numerically near-equivalent and this is fastText's default, but it is not the hierarchical softmax the paper names; it does not affect the target metric.
thread=20 with fastText's asynchronous multi-threaded SGD and lrUpdateRate=100, giving the paper's linearly decaying learning rate (the log shows lr decaying 0.5 -> 0.0 across the epoch).
dim=10, epoch=5, and a real grid search over {0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5} on a held-out validation split (selected lr=0.5; per-lr validation accuracies 91.17/92.27/92.21/92.28).
A single shared configuration is used and only AG News is exercised (the match target's dataset), so cross-dataset consistency of hyperparameters cannot be verified from this run.

bucket=10,000,000 is used although the target row has unigrams+bigrams (paper Sec. 2.2 would imply 100M). The implementer justifies this by the authors' classification-results.sh and a ~4 GB memory limit; it is explicitly disclosed in the notes.

Data is the Zhang et al. (2015) AG News release (120k train / 7.6k test) and conversion is an exact port of the authors' normalize_text(); train/test counts and label balance (30000/1900 per class) are checked in intermediate_checks.
Tag-prediction (YFCC100M, h=200, precision@1) was not run; it is outside the C1 match target, so this is expected.
Training used thread=20 as stated in Sec. 3.1 (config.THREAD=20; metrics note records the authors' shell script uses 4).
model.test() uses the trained model's efficient tree/softmax prediction to return the top-1 class on the 7,600-example test split.
